newsitem.title: UK: NWE spot gas oil slides with IPE, premiums weaken.
newsitem.headline: NWE spot gas oil slides with IPE, premiums weaken.

text.p: NWE gas oil outright prices slid by up to $8 a tonne, extending Friday's losses, in thin trade on Monday, traders said.

Traders attributed much of the fall to sharply weaker benchmark gas oil futures although they said high ARA stocks and slack demand from the key German inland market had also depressed prompt premiums, rubbing out the small physical backwardation for heating oil.
"Buyers can stay relaxed," one trader said. "The downside volatility on futures, high ARA stocks and forecast warmer weather all favour them."
Russian cargo premiums weakened $1 to around Feb IPE +1 a tonne, pressured by an armada of cargoes scheduled to load at Ventspils in the first decade of February.
Traders said some of the oil may head trans-Atlantic but much is expected to be moved into NWE storage.
Prompt barges were valued Feb IPE +$1 per tonne slipping to around parity for late Feb loadings.
In contrast to heating oil, diesel premiums held steady with barges for Germany valued around Feb IPE +$9 fob NWE while cif cargoes talked Feb IPE +$18/21 a tonne CIF NWE.
